title: Mate in three: the same list, one round deeper
outcomes: Follows a first move through each reply to the mate in three
Counts the king's legal moves after the first move before following a line
Rejects a mate in three that one extra king square breaks
Says "no forced mate in three" when a promising check fails

steps.text: A **mate in three** adds one more round: your move, their reply, your move, their reply, mate. Use the same list at each of your turns. After your first move, test the defender's forcing replies first: a check, the capture of your attacking piece, a move that gives the king a square. *Rule of thumb:* count the replies after the first move. If there are only one or two, follow each to the end.

steps.caption: White to move. Bxc5+ starts a mate in three. Count the king's moves after each check.

line.say: Check. The black king has one legal move.
Check again, along the long diagonal.
The bishop takes the blocker. Checkmate.

claims.statement: After Bxc5+ the black king has one legal move.

steps.text: **Where the search breaks.** The defender has more chances: a check, the capture of your attacking piece, or a king square you did not count. One extra square can end the line. *Rule of thumb:* after the first move, count the king's squares and the defender's checks before following any line. A strong attack is not a mate: if the list runs out, say "no forced mate" and look for another plan.

steps.title: One bishop moved
steps.prompt: In the first position Bxc5+ forces mate in three. Now one black piece stands elsewhere. Predict, then check.

steps.text: No labels now. In each position decide whether there is a forced mate in three. The next three exercises are silent: no hints and no engine line until you answer.

steps.prompt: In the last exercise, did you follow every reply to the end, or stop when the first one worked? In your own games, the next time you see a strong attack, write down the king's squares and the defender's checks before you commit.

fields.label: Did you follow every reply to the end?
What did you miss, if anything? (one line)
